title: Pilot Partner Non-Production Data Scope & Staging Agreement (working draft)
content:
Purpose:
This working draft frames a lightweight contract module for short-term pilot customers where only non-production (staging/sandbox/test) datasets are processed by Redwood-managed inference. Goal is rapid partner enablement while setting clear minimal legal and evidence requirements for risk-limited pilots. NOT meant for production or PHI/regulated use — see NOTES and exclusions below.

High-level summary (one line):
Provide a short-term, limited-scope Data Processing & Staging Agreement that limits liability, defines non-production data handling, prescribes minimal evidence and audit posture, and allows a quick path to production-grade DPA or Dedicated contract.

Scope & applicability:
- Parties: Redwood Inference ("Provider") and Pilot Partner ("Customer").
- Covered activity: processing of Customer-supplied non-production data for the sole purpose of testing, integration, model evaluation, or UI/UX verification in Provider-managed staging environments.
- Explicit exclusion: any data classified by Customer as "regulated", "sensitive personal data", PCI, PHI, or production PII. Customer must label data and confirm non-production status prior to ingestion.
- Duration: pilot term (default 30 days) unless amended in writing. Auto-expire unless renewed.

Definitions (quick):
- "Non-Production Data": datasets explicitly marked by Customer as sandbox, synthetic, redacted, or test-only.
- "Ephemeral Logs": runtime request/response logs retained only for debugging; separate retention rule applies.
- "Evidence Package": minimal artifacts Provider will produce upon request for the pilot (see Evidence Requirements).

Data handling & isolation requirements:
- Segregation: pilot workloads must run in a distinct staging namespace/cluster with logical isolation from production fleets. Provider will use separate storage buckets or labeled prefixes.
- Access controls: only named Provider engineers and the Customer's nominated contacts have access; role-based access and just-in-time (JIT) privileges recommended.
- Inference telemetry: by default, Provider will collect minimal telemetry (latency, errors, throughput). Customer must opt-in in writing for request/response capture.
- KV/prefix cache: Provider will disable cross-customer persistent prefix caching for pilot namespaces.

Retention & deletion:
- Ephemeral Logs: retained by Provider for up to 14 days by default; Customer may request shorter retention in writing.
- Uploaded artifacts (datasets/models): retained for the term plus 7 days for handoff; deleted thereafter unless Customer requests export.
- Deletion proof: Provider will provide deletion confirmation (timestamp + object ids) as the primary evidence. Full forensic proofs reserved for production DPA.

Evidence & audit-lite commitments:
Provider commits to produce the following Evidence Package within 7 business days of a Customer request during the term:
- List of staging namespace identifiers and active nodes that processed the Customer's workload.
- Deletion confirmations for any uploaded objects.
- Incident summary for any security events affecting the staging namespace.
Limitations: no deep forensics or source-code-level artifacts for pilots; those require escalation and a separate MSA/SOW.

Subprocessors & tooling:
- Provider may use third-party cloud infra and managed services (compute, storage, telemetry). Provider will maintain a short subprocessors list for pilots and surface any high‑risk subprocessors proactively.
- Customer may request temporary disablement of selected telemetry or third-party integrations during the pilot; Provider will evaluate feasibility.

Security baseline (minimum expectations):
- Network isolation (VPC or logical equivalent), TLS in transit, role-based access, and limited retention as per this doc.
- Provider to perform a basic pre-launch configuration checklist (See TODO checklist below).

Liability & indemnity (pilot-limited):
- Cap: aggregate liability for the pilot is limited to the fees paid by Customer for the pilot period or $50,000, whichever is lower.
- No consequential damages; standard carveouts for gross negligence and willful misconduct.
- Indemnity: Customer remains responsible for ensuring data they label non-production is accurately classified; Provider is not liable for Customer-misclassified regulated data ingested into pilot.

Incident notification & response:
- Provider will notify Customer within 48 hours of any confirmed security event that impacts Customer's staging namespace.
- Triage call: within 24 hours of notification a conference call will be scheduled with named contacts.
- Remediation: Provider will apply mitigations and provide an incident brief within 7 business days.

Termination & transition:
- On expiry/termination, Provider will stop processing and either delete Customer artifacts or provide export instructions.
- Transition window: 7 days for export by default.
- If Customer wishes to convert to production/longer term, parties must execute a production DPA and (if needed) Dedicated contract.

Operational checklist (working):
- [ ] Confirm Customer non-production data labeling and get signed attestation.
- [ ] Create isolated staging namespace and record namespace id.
- [ ] Disable cross-customer persistent caches for namespace.
- [ ] Configure retention (default ephemeral logs 14 days).
- [ ] Document named Provider and Customer contacts and Slack channel.
- [ ] Run security pre-launch checklist (link to Confluence).

Open questions / negotiation points (notes to self):
- Should we allow customers to bring their own KMS for staging buckets? operationally possible but increases setup time.
- Is 14 days for logs acceptable for most Pilot partners? consider 7-day alternative for higher sensitivity.
- Evidence depth: can we offer an optional "pilot+" package that includes signed deletion attestations and a short SOC-style evidence packet for an added fee?

Placeholders & negotiable fields (for template):
- “Pilot Term”: [30 days]
- “Retention for Ephemeral Logs”: [14 days]
- “Liability Cap”: [fees paid] or [$50,000]
- “Customer Attestation Link”: [Customer to provide signed attestation confirming non-production status]

References & links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Pilot+Data+Handling (working draft)
- Jira: SEC-457 (pilot contract template backlog)
- Slack: #sec-pilot-onboarding (channel for operational handoffs)
- GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pilot-contract-templates (template source)

Sign-off / next steps:
- Legal to review liability language and indemnity carveouts (assign to Legal: Elena M.)
- Product/security to validate operational checklist (Priya D.)
- Engage Solutions Eng for onboarding runbook and expected lead time (assign: Liam O.).

Version history (working):
- 2024-11-05 initial draft (Samir K.).
- 2024-11-12 updated evidence commitments and retention defaults (Priya D.).
- 2024-11-18 adjusted liability cap language and added checklist items (Elena M.).

Notes: this is intentionally "lightweight" to enable fast pilots. For any pilot that touches regulated data or expects multi-week retention or production SLA guarantees, escalate to standard DPA + Dedicated terms.
